text: The technical steps of a community speaker's domain consolidation included submitting new sitemaps, filing a change of address in Search Console and updating internal links so the new pages did not rely on redirects alone.

session: Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves
speaker: Martyna Ağanoğlu
label: stage

session: What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet.
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Markup for schema.org types that Google does not use yet is a bet on future features; check a type's usage bucket on schema.org before investing, since adoption is what Google says it watches before building a feature.

session: What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet.
speaker: Ryan Levering
label: slide
text: Google announced server-side structured data validation as coming soon: it will publish downloadable validation rules in SHACL on each structured data feature guide, with other kinds of checks to follow.

session: What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet.
speaker: Ryan Levering
label: slide
text: Google's planned validation workflow has five steps: download the rules from the feature guide, generate the JSON or embedded microdata or RDFa, run the rules against the generated server-side markup as a first check, deploy and test in the Rich Results Test, and monitor ongoing performance in Search Console.

session: What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet.
speaker: Ryan Levering
label: stage
text: The SHACL rules are meant to run inside a site's content generation, so markup is sanity-checked before it is published and does not silently regress later, a breakage site owners might otherwise discover only through a Search Console report.

session: What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet.
speaker: Ryan Levering
label: stage
text: The SHACL rules will not replace Search Console as the canonical place for structured data reports, because some checks use Google's internal libraries and cannot be expressed in SHACL, but they will catch problems such as a missing required field.

session: What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet.
speaker: Ryan Levering
label: slide
text: Google's example SHACL shape for Event requires a name, treats a missing description only as a warning, and accepts the image either as an ImageObject or as a URL.

session: What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet.
speaker: Ryan Levering
label: stage
text: Google plans a SHACL rule set for each of its structured data feature types and will release the rule sets gradually once they have been checked.

session: What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet.
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: When the SHACL rules appear, wire them into the build or CMS publishing step as an automated test, so a template change that drops a required property fails before deployment instead of surfacing weeks later in Search Console.

session: What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet.
speaker: Ryan Levering
label: stage
text: Structured data makes pages eligible to appear as rich results, Google's structured data talk said in its recap.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos

label: stage

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: Google supports the picture element only because a picture element must contain an img element, and that img element is what Google extracts and passes to its media indexer.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: One of the most reliable ways to make sure Google finds an image is to include it in an img element in the HTML; Gary Illyes named image sitemaps as the other method.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
author: Google Search Central
label: docs
text: Google's documented ways to keep a site's images out of search results are a robots.txt disallow rule (for example for Googlebot-Image) or a noindex X-Robots-Tag HTTP header, with the Removals tool for emergencies.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Hiding an image as a CSS background is a fragile way to keep it out of Google: it only stops extraction from that page, so the same image URL used in an img element elsewhere or listed in a sitemap can still be indexed; the documented robots.txt or noindex X-Robots-Tag methods are the reliable route.

sources.title: Remove images hosted on your site from search results

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: Of the attributes the HTML standard defines for the img element, Google uses three and ignores the rest; Gary Illyes named src and alt but not the third.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: The src attribute is the most important img attribute, because without it Google does not know where the image bytes are and cannot index the image.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: Gary Illyes ranked the alt attribute below src in importance, while saying alt attributes are still important.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
author: Google Search Central
label: docs
text: Google's image SEO guide calls alt text the most important attribute for providing more metadata about an image, and says Google uses it together with computer vision and the page content to understand the image.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: Alt text should describe the image in words for someone who cannot see it.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: Google uses the words in an alt attribute to understand the image, may attach them to the image at serving time, and the image can rank for concepts the alt text describes.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: The text around an image is critical: Google uses it as context to understand the image and to rank it, so an alt attribute alone is not enough.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Images that should rank need an img element with a real src; hero or product images set as CSS backgrounds are invisible to Google Images and image features, so keep CSS backgrounds for decorative images you do not need indexed.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Give important images a caption or explanatory sentence next to them rather than relying on alt text alone, since Gary Illyes ranked src above alt and called the surrounding text critical for ranking the image.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: Besides img elements, image sitemaps tell Google about images: they are XML sitemaps that list, under a page's loc entry, the locations of the images on that page.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
author: Google Search Central, Search Central blog (30 August 2024)
label: docs
text: Google's image SEO guide lists AVIF among the supported image formats (with BMP, GIF, JPEG, PNG, WebP and SVG), and Google announced in August 2024 that AVIF files need nothing special to be indexed.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: Use high-quality modern image formats such as WebP for a good balance of quality and compression, and keep image files small so people can enjoy them.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: While the AVIF ingestion hiccup Gary Illyes mentioned lasts, serve AVIF only through source elements inside picture and keep a WebP or JPEG file in the img src, which is the URL Google extracts, even though Google's documentation lists AVIF as supported; then check in Google Images that key images appear.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes

speaker: Gary Illyes

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos

label: slide

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: slide

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: slide

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: slide
text: Including videos in a sitemap helps Google discover all of a site's video content.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Give each important video its own watch page where the video is the main content, add VideoObject markup and list the video in a video sitemap; a video buried in a long article lacks the dedicated watch page that Google listed as a key factor.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos

speaker: Gary Illyes

speaker: Gary Illyes

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: Serving videos from a content delivery network (CDN) that loads them faster than the site's own server is a win for video SEO, Gary Illyes said.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: Google supports the most popular video file formats on the web.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: Encode videos with standard codecs, because some people will not be able to play videos that use unusual ones.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: For a video to be discovered it must be embedded prominently, above the fold; Gary Illyes said a video placed below the fold is not going to be indexed.
quote: If it's not above the fold, then you basically lost the game.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: Video sitemaps are not critical but good to have, because Google ingests video sitemaps much more often than it can process HTML pages.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: A video sitemap or video feed tells Google which URLs carry videos so it can visit those URLs to double-check; without one, Google has to check every page individually.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: Descriptive text around a video helps Google rank and retrieve the video.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: Google's media indexer processes the images and videos that feature extraction passes to it and attaches them to the URL of the page that hosts them.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: Googlebot-Image and Googlebot-Video are the Google crawlers that fetch images and videos, and robots.txt rules addressed to their user agent tokens control how Google indexes a site's images and videos.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes

speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
speaker: Gary Illyes

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos

text: Gary Illyes showed a timeline image that Google made with an image generation model in 2025 and deliberately left unfixed as a counterexample: its text was garbled and its years jumped from 1994 to 1995 and back to 1994.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos

author: Google Search Console Help

text: Google's Video indexing report help says only videos on a watch page are eligible for indexing, and flags 'Cannot determine video position and size' when the player is not on the page at load, for example behind a click-to-play image, asking for the player to load at its real size and position without user interaction.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
author: Google Search Central

text: Google's image metadata guide says Google Images supports the IPTC Digital Source Type values for algorithmically created images, such as trainedAlgorithmicMedia, and can show C2PA details in 'About this image', such as whether an image was created or edited with AI tools.

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos

session: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
