session: Welcome to serving and ranking day!
speaker: Google
label: slide
text: Google's opening slide for serving day showed serving as the third stage after crawling and indexing, and drew Google's serving infrastructure as query understanding and retrieval leading into the index, then ranking and search features leading back to the user, for the example query 'Where to eat jamon'.

sources.title: In-depth guide to how Google Search works

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google's query understanding talk set out to show how the changes Google makes to users' queries relate to what a website can provide.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: A Google speaker said that a messy query, made of a hotel location copied from a website plus a question about Italian food, was figured out by Google's systems, which came up with answers for it.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google placed query understanding in the traditional part of Search, the part where answers are looked up in an index and then presented and ranked.

sources.title: In-depth guide to how Google Search works

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google said it has no name for traditional, non-AI Search, only for its Search generative AI features, and that the two play together but are easier to understand separately.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google's first step in understanding almost any query is to detect its language, which tells Google roughly what content the user wants: a query in German suggests German content, a query in English English content.

sources.title: How Google knows what language to show in search results

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Query language detection works poorly when someone searches only for a brand name, such as Facebook or Google, because the query does not show which language the user wants results in.

sources.title: How Google knows what language to show in search results

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: For brand-only queries Google falls back on other information, such as the user's location and browser settings, to work out the language of the results.

sources.title: How Google knows what language to show in search results
Tell Google about localized versions of your page

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Because a brand-only query does not reveal the user's language, Google sometimes struggles to show the right language version of a page for brand searches.

sources.title: How Google knows what language to show in search results

author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Sites with several language versions should not leave brand searches to chance: annotate the versions with hreflang and offer a visible language switcher, because Google may have only the user's location and browser settings to choose a version.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google named Thai as a language that makes query understanding more complex because it does not separate words with spaces; the speaker added, hedging with 'apparently', that Thai uses spaces to separate sentences.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: After detecting the query language and separating the words, Google removes words it thinks matter little to the query, such as 'a' and 'of', known as stop words.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google's query processing deliberately mirrors indexing: a query is transformed into something that can be matched against the index, and stop word removal is part of that transformation.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: For some searches the stop words are important, and Google then tries to recognise the whole phrase, stop words included, as an entity; in indexing, such words are indexed together.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google said the difference between words and entities can be seen in Google Trends, where a term can be searched as words or as an entity (Trends calls these a search term and a topic).

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: When a query names an entity, Google treats it as a request for that entity rather than as a collection of separate words.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: In ranking, Google can match a query's words or its entity, and, the speaker said with a 'probably', mixes both to some degree.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google expands queries with synonyms in traditional Search; the speaker compared this to query fan-out but said it is part of traditional Search, not of the AI features.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: In Google's example, the query word 'photograph' could be expanded to 'image', 'picture' or 'photo', but one German candidate had to be dropped because the similar German word means 'photographer', so expansions are language-specific.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: According to Google's ranking teams, the synonym system is one of the most important parts of how Google handles a query.
quote: they say that the synonym system is one of the most important parts

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Synonyms matter because users often phrase a query differently from the way content is indexed; synonym expansion makes the words Google looks up findable in its index.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: For technical terms, Google's synonym swapping can return either a technical page or a simplified page for the same query.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Site owners do not need to list all synonyms of a term on a page, because Google already knows the synonyms and looks for them on pages too.
quote: you don't have to do that SEO meme of, like, list all the synonyms on your page

author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Write each page in the words its audience uses and drop synonym lists added for search engines: Google adds synonyms at query time, and blocks of keyword variants read as keyword stuffing, which Google's spam policies prohibit.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google adds alternative words to a query automatically, which the speaker compared to a user joining words with the OR search operator.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google suggested a test: a search that lists a term's synonyms joined with OR will probably return results very similar to the plain query, because Google adds the synonyms itself (part of the sentence is unclear in the recording).

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Googlers write queries in brackets, for example [spicy cheese store near me], so when reporting a search problem to a Googler, putting the query in brackets shows that it is a query someone searched.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google rewrites pretty much every query, through synonym expansion and in other ways, to understand better what the query means.
quote: pretty much all queries are rewritten

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Internally, a short query can turn into a much longer rewritten query, because Google adds entities, synonyms and other information before looking it up.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: In Google's rewrite example, [fried chicken place in Barcelona] keeps 'fried' and 'chicken' as two words, may add an entity for fried chicken, and replaces 'place' with alternatives such as 'area', 'location' or 'restaurant'.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Some alternatives in a rewritten query make no sense, such as 'fried chicken area in Barcelona', which is harmless because few indexed pages match them.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: In a rewritten query, a place name such as Barcelona can stay a word or be swapped for an entity, possibly a more specific location.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: For a query containing 'near me', Google understands that the user wants results near their location, not pages containing the words 'near me', and rewrites the query accordingly.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Some synonyms are contextual and depend on the rest of the query: 'GM' probably means General Motors in [GM car], general manager in [GM restaurants] and genetically modified in [GM barley].

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google builds its synonyms as automatically as possible, behind the scenes, rather than having linguists catalogue every language and all possible synonyms.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google's synonyms need not be synonyms linguistically: words people use interchangeably are treated as synonyms, because the aim is to find the right content in the index.
quote: we don't need to be technically accurate

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: When Google highlights a word in its results that looks like the wrong synonym, the reason is probably that many people use the two words interchangeably.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Besides synonyms, Google detects 'siblings', words in the same category that are related but not interchangeable, such as Canon and Nikon.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Because Canon and Nikon are siblings rather than synonyms, a search for [Canon camera] should not show Nikon cameras.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google learns synonyms and siblings from search behaviour: words people search with in the same way become synonyms, while frequent comparison queries mark words as not interchangeable (the end of the sentence is unclear in the recording).

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google does not prefer English words on pages in other languages; the idea that Google, as an American company, wants to see everything in English is wrong.

sources.title: How Google knows what language to show in search results

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Where Google recognises an English term and its local-language equivalent as synonyms, a page does not need to contain both.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: To check whether Google treats two terms as the same, search for each: [Iberico ham] and [jamón ibérico] both brought up the same entity, so Google understands them as the same thing.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: When Google already matches a term's variants, there is no need to add them to pages artificially; mention another name only where visitors might not understand otherwise.
quote: I wouldn't artificially just stuff those variations in there.

sources.title: Spam policies for Google web search

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: At the time of the talk, a search for [Spanish cured ham] brought up mainly a Wikipedia page, showing that Google does not automatically equate that phrase with Iberico ham.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: When Google does not treat a phrase as a synonym, such as 'Spanish cured ham' for Iberico ham, a page that wants to cover that phrase should use it in its text.

author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Before writing, search for each variant of a key term: if the variants bring up the same entity or near-identical results, use the term your audience uses; if one variant returns unrelated results, write that variant on the page.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google generally treats spellings with and without diacritics as synonyms behind the scenes, for example a German 'ü' written as 'ü', as 'ue' or left out.

sources.title: How search results may differ based on accented characters and interface languages

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google sometimes gets diacritic variants wrong, so it is worth searching to see whether Google understands a variant; if it does, pick one spelling and use it.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google's recommendation for diacritics, non-English words, product names and spelling variants is to focus first on what users actually search for.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Users expect content written the way they search: in some languages they search in Latin characters, in others in the local script, and Hindi users, for example, search both in Hindi and in Latin letters.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google said focusing on what users actually do makes more sense than trying to match what the search engine does.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Spelling variants need no artificial focus: users are often fine finding one version of a word on one page and another version elsewhere.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google advised double-checking any word you are unsure about by searching for it on Google and looking at what comes up.

author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: For audiences that type the same words in two scripts or spellings (Hindi in Devanagari and in Latin letters, German with and without umlauts), check which forms appear in Search Console's queries and use those forms in headings and key text.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google's generative AI features in Search build on the traditional ways of searching, so query understanding also flows into AI Overviews and AI Mode.

sources.title: Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search

speaker: John Mueller
label: slide
text: Google's slide on how LLM features with grounding generally work showed a query going to both the search engine and an LLM, the search engine's results going to the LLM, the LLM generating fan-out queries that go back to the search engine, and the LLM returning answers with links.
quote: How LLM features with grounding generally work

sources.title: Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: In Google's AI features, the query and the search results are additionally sent to an LLM, which returns new queries for Google to run.

sources.title: Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google treats fan-out queries generated by the LLM the same way as queries typed by users, so understanding how normal queries work explains fan-out queries too.

sources.title: Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google said a short video showing how one query is expanded into several fan-out queries has been in its documentation for a while.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google tries to make fan-out queries distinct from each other for better coverage, avoiding asking the same question several times, which would return the same answers.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Every fan-out query goes through Google's query understanding, including synonym expansion.

sources.title: Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Google said fan-out queries are not added to Search Console, because Google considers them part of its infrastructure.
quote: Fan-out queries are not added in Search Console, because they're basically a part of our infrastructure.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Individual fan-out queries can be seen in some other places, such as Gemini, some search APIs and other LLM systems.

sources.title: Grounding with Google Search
sources.publisher: Google AI for Developers (Gemini API docs)

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: Because every system runs fan-out differently, Google advised understanding that fan-out happens but not overfocusing on individual fan-out queries or on how to rank for them.
quote: I would not overfocus on which individual fan-out queries happen and how can I rank for those

sources.title: Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search

author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Do not build pages for fan-out queries copied from Gemini or other LLM tools: they differ from system to system and Search Console does not report them. Cover a topic's real subquestions on solid pages instead.

speaker: John Mueller
label: slide
text: Google's summary slide on query understanding told site owners not to worry about typos and plurals, which Google rewrites automatically.
quote: Don't worry about typos & plurals!

speaker: John Mueller
label: slide
text: Google's summary slide on query understanding said that synonyms are expanded automatically.

speaker: John Mueller
label: slide
text: Google's summary slide on query understanding said Google's synonyms are not always language-based; on stage this was explained as words people use interchangeably counting as synonyms even when they are not synonyms linguistically.
quote: Google's synonyms aren't always language-based

speaker: John Mueller
label: slide
text: Google's summary slide on query understanding noted that some languages do not use spaces between words, which complicates query understanding.

speaker: John Mueller
label: slide
text: Google's summary slide on query understanding said query fan-out does even more expansion than synonym expansion.

sources.title: Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search

speaker: John Mueller
label: slide
text: Google's summary slide on query understanding concluded that all this query expansion gives site owners many opportunities for their content to be found and shown.
quote: There are many opportunities to find and show your content.

speaker: John Mueller
label: stage
text: After query understanding and expansion, Google sends the queries to the index to look up pages, the retrieval step.

sources.title: In-depth guide to how Google Search works

speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: Google's index uses posting lists: for each word, a list of the URLs associated with that word.

speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: At retrieval, Google splits the query into words, applies query understanding and expansion, and matches the words and their expansions against the posting lists.

speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: For retrieval, Google uses signals attached individually to each document in the index.

sources.title: In-depth guide to how Google Search works

speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: The first condition for retrieving a document is that the query's words, or its concepts in the case of vectors or embeddings, are in the document or related to it.

speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: Because a query like [best fried chicken ever] can match millions of pages, Google already orders the candidates during retrieval, before ranking starts.

speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: To order candidates at retrieval, Google uses signals collected during indexing, and the first two are language and country.

sources.title: In-depth guide to how Google Search works

speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: At retrieval, Google tries to match results to the user's language wherever possible: someone searching in Spanish does not necessarily want results in Italian.

speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: Where Google cannot find results in the user's language, the speaker called the gap an opportunity for whoever targets those words.

speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: Country is the second retrieval signal: a user searching from Switzerland wants cheese from Switzerland, not from Germany, and a user in Spain is poorly served by results targeting a South American country.

sources.title: In-depth guide to how Google Search works

speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: Google called quality the most important of the signals used to order candidates at retrieval: a URL of high quality is more likely to be retrieved from the index for specific queries.
quote: if the quality of a URL is high, then it's more likely to be retrieved from the index for specific queries.

speaker: Gary Illyes
label: stage
text: The same quality signal that Google uses at retrieval is also used in ranking when results are served.

sources.title: In-depth guide to how Google Search works

author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Quality acts twice: a page Google judges low in quality is less likely to be retrieved as a candidate at all, so it may never reach ranking, which makes content quality a precondition rather than a final tweak.

author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Make each page's language and target country unambiguous (one main language per page, hreflang between versions, local prices, addresses and shipping details), because Google applies language and country already at retrieval, before ranking.

author: Google Search (How Search Works)
label: docs
text: Google's How Search Works page says understanding a query ranges from recognising and correcting spelling mistakes to a synonym system that finds relevant documents without the exact words searched, such as 'adjust laptop brightness' for 'change laptop brightness'.

author: Google Search (How Search Works)
label: docs
text: Google's How Search Works page says the language models it builds to match a query's few words to the most useful content took over five years to develop and significantly improve results in over 30% of searches across languages.

author: Google Search Central
label: docs
text: Google's SEO Starter Guide advises anticipating the different words readers search with (some search for 'charcuterie', others for 'cheese board') but not worrying about every variation, because Google's language matching systems relate pages to queries without the exact terms.

author: Google Search Help
label: docs
text: Google's Search Help says the language of search results is chosen from the language of the query, the user's Google language setting, the device's languages and the user's location, which helps when a word such as 'taxi' is the same in several languages.

sources.title: How Google knows what language to show in search results

author: Search Central blog (1 September 2006)
label: docs
text: A 2006 Search Central blog post says Google considers pages with and without accents for a query word (México and Mexico), and that which accented characters count as equivalent depends on the searcher's interface language.

sources.title: How search results may differ based on accented characters and interface languages

author: Google Search Central
label: docs
text: Google's guide to multi-regional and multilingual sites says Google Search tries to find pages that match the language of the searcher, and that geotargeting a site to one country can improve its rankings there at the expense of other locales.

author: Google Search Console Help
label: docs
text: Google's Search Console help says AI Mode groups the user's question into subtopics and searches for each one simultaneously, and that a follow-up question in AI Mode is essentially a new query.

sources.title: What are impressions, position, and clicks?

author: Google AI for Developers (Gemini API docs)
label: docs
text: Google's Gemini API documentation on grounding with Google Search says the model automatically generates and runs one or more search queries when needed, and the response lists the search queries it executed.

sources.title: Grounding with Google Search
sources.publisher: Google AI for Developers (Gemini API docs)

author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: No Google documentation states that fan-out queries stay out of Search Console, but the docs fit the stage statement: the Performance report counts AI Overviews and AI Mode under the user's own queries, and the Generative AI reports have no query dimension.

sources.title: What are impressions, position, and clicks?
Introducing Search Generative AI performance reports in Search Console

author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: The retrieval talk went further than Google's documentation, which says Search returns the highest-quality and most relevant results and lists quality among key ranking signals, but never describes quality as deciding which pages are retrieved from the index at all.

sources.title: In-depth guide to how Google Search works

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality
speaker: Community speakers
label: stage
text: In Lightning session K (Facets of quality), a community speaker argued that SEO is for humans: write for people and the problems they have, rather than to please Googlebot.
quote: SEO is for humans

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality
speaker: Community speakers
label: stage
text: A community speaker recalled that around 2009 writers bent titles and phrases to include a keyword because their CMS counted keyword density, and said that hitting the ratio really worked at the time.

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Do not treat keyword-density or word-count scores from CMS plugins as editorial targets: Google's spam policies treat filling a page with keywords to manipulate rankings as keyword stuffing, and Google says it has no preferred word count.

sources.title: Spam policies for Google web search

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality
author: Google Search Central
label: docs
text: Google's spam policies define keyword stuffing as filling a web page with keywords or numbers to manipulate rankings in Google Search, for example repeating the same words or phrases so often that it sounds unnatural.
quote: filling a web page with keywords or numbers in an attempt to manipulate rankings in Google Search results

sources.title: Spam policies for Google web search

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality
author: Google Search Central
label: docs
text: Google's guide to people-first content lists writing to a particular word count, in the belief that Google prefers one, as a warning sign of search engine-first content, and says Google has no preferred word count.
quote: Google has a preferred word count? (No, we don't.)

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality
speaker: Community speakers
label: stage
text: Entering the Polish market late, against strong competition and with a small team, a community speaker's team could not be a 'department store' that covers everything, so it went really deep instead of going broad.

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality
author: Google Search Central
label: docs
text: Google's guide to people-first content lists producing lots of content on many different topics, in the hope that some of it performs well in search results, as a warning sign of search engine-first content.

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality
speaker: Community speakers
label: stage
text: To choose what to cover in depth, a community speaker's team used Google Trends to find what people in their market were interested in and then gave them that content.

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality
speaker: Community speakers
label: stage
text: A community speaker reported that going deep instead of broad took the Polish edition of a large Spanish software-download website into the top three technology websites in Poland (period not stated).

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality
speaker: Community speakers
label: stage
text: With a much smaller team, the Polish edition of a large Spanish software-download website reached double the organic traffic of the site's English edition, a community speaker reported (period and measure not stated).

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality
speaker: Community speakers
label: stage
text: Because Googlebot is not a human, the speaker's team at the time thought more about Googlebot than about human readers, a community speaker said.

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality
speaker: Community speakers
label: stage
text: A community speaker compared Googlebot to an inspector who cannot enter the shop and only looks through the window, seeing the page as ones and zeros, which the speaker linked to tokenization.

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: The inspector metaphor blends two steps: Googlebot fetches pages during crawling, while tokenization happens later when the page is processed for the index, as Google explained on Day 2.

sources.title: In-depth guide to how Google Search works

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality
speaker: Community speakers
label: stage
text: Because a bot that counts things was easy to work around, SEOs made the facade of their sites nice and fancy instead of focusing on what was inside, sometimes with no real shop behind the facade, a community speaker said.

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality
speaker: Community speakers
label: stage
text: Google updates such as Panda and Penguin made Google steadily better at seeing past the facade of a site, a community speaker said.

sources.title: A guide to Google Search ranking systems

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality
author: Google Search Central
label: docs
text: Google's ranking systems guide lists Panda as a retired system: announced in 2011 to better ensure that high-quality and original content appears in search results, it became part of the core ranking systems in 2015.

sources.title: A guide to Google Search ranking systems

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality
author: Google Search Central
label: docs
text: Google's ranking systems guide lists Penguin as a retired system: announced in 2012 to combat link spam, it was integrated into the core ranking systems in 2016.

sources.title: A guide to Google Search ranking systems

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Of the two updates named on stage as letting Google see past a site's facade, only Panda targeted content quality; Penguin targeted link spam, and both have been part of Google's core ranking systems since 2015 and 2016, so neither runs as a separate system today.

sources.title: A guide to Google Search ranking systems

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality
speaker: Community speakers
label: stage
text: With AI, Google can finally look inside the shop and check how a page's content matches its storefront, a community speaker said.

sources.title: A guide to Google Search ranking systems

session: Lightning session K: Facets of quality

speaker: Gary Illyes

text: Google described its search results page as an auction system in which the individual results, of different types, all bid for a place on the page; the auction is a metaphor for result types competing for space, not a reference to ads.

speaker: Gary Illyes

speaker: Gary Illyes

label: stage
text: Google decided against adding hundreds of thousands of highly specific feed attributes, such as heel height for shoes or lens details for cameras, and instead added a few flexible ones that leave merchants in control.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Google Shopping said highly prescriptive product data is a lot of hard work for merchants and is no longer needed for LLMs.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Google added six Merchant Center feed attributes for AI shopping experiences: question and answer, documents, related products, item group title and variant option for variants, and popularity rank.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Google's January 2026 announcement spoke of 'dozens' of new Merchant Center attributes, while the Day 3 talk counted six; all six named on stage (question_and_answer, document_link, related_product, item_group_title, variant_option, popularity_rank) are in the Merchant Center product data specification as of 3 October 2026.

sources.title: New tech and tools for retailers to succeed in an agentic shopping era

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
author: Google Merchant Center Help
label: docs
text: Google's Merchant Center help marks the question_and_answer, document_link, related_product and popularity_rank attributes as primarily intended for conversational experiences such as AI Mode in Google Search.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: The question and answer feed attribute lets a merchant or brand upload questions and answers relevant to a product, whether they come from the manufacturer or from consumers.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
author: Google Merchant Center Help
label: docs
text: Merchant Center's question_and_answer attribute takes up to 30 question-and-answer pairs per product, each question and answer up to 1,000 characters and 10,000 characters in total, and must not contain prices, shipping, dates or the company name.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Merchants can now provide a document describing a product, such as a PDF manual, a spec sheet or the package contents, so that AI can work out what the product is about.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
author: Google Merchant Center Help
label: docs
text: Merchant Center's document_link attribute takes up to five URLs of PDF documents about a product, such as manuals, user guides or assembly instructions, and the merchant must own the content licensing rights.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: The related products feed attribute describes accessories, parts and replacement products, answering frequent questions such as what else to buy with a printer.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Variant data in Google's feed specification used to be limited to basics such as colour and size; the new item group title and variant option attributes make it much more flexible.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Google added a popularity rank feed attribute because consumers want to know how well a product sells on a marketplace.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
author: Google Merchant Center Help
label: docs
text: Merchant Center's popularity_rank is a 0-100 value the merchant assigns to rank a product's popularity, based on its recent sales, against the rest of its own inventory; it does not reflect user ratings.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: On stage the popularity rank was framed as how well a product sells on a marketplace, but Google's documentation defines it as the merchant's own 0-100 ranking against the rest of its inventory: a self-reported, relative value, not a sales figure across shops.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Product Q&A data lets AI answer very detailed questions, such as a kettle's temperature settings, capacity or keep-warm safety, that separate feed attributes could never represent; Google's example came from a real merchant's product.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Google Shopping called rich data with light structure the AI sweet spot: a little structure that helps the AI system understand the data, not deep, highly nested, complex structures.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Some structure is much better than none for AI systems, because without structure the model does not really know what is going on, Google Shopping said.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Most of the new conversational feed attributes were already available in schema.org, so Google ties them back to structured data and can use them from product markup as well as from feeds.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: As of 3 October 2026 Google's Merchant Center help lists no schema.org property for question_and_answer, document_link, related_product, popularity_rank, variant_option or product_detail (only item_group_title maps, to ProductGroup.name), and Search Central does not document such markup: reading these attributes from schema.org is a stage statement, the feed is the documented route.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Basic product markup has two parts: product data that is the same for every merchant (name, description, brand, images) and offer data specific to one merchant's offer (URL, condition, availability, price).

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: In product markup, an offer's shipping and return information can point through a JSON-LD identifier (@id) to shipping and return data defined elsewhere.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
author: Google Search Central
label: docs
text: Google's merchant listing documentation recommends defining shipping and return policies once under Organization markup and referencing them from an Offer, even on another page, using only the @id keyword (through hasShippingService for shipping, hasMerchantReturnPolicy for returns).

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Google Shopping uses its own crawler, Storebot (Storebot-Google), instead of Googlebot because it needs fresh product information, prices, availability and shipping details and therefore crawls much more often.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Storebot-Google is used to validate merchant feeds: when a feed gives a price, Google double-checks it on the merchant's site.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Storebot-Google also does deep crawls, for example of checkout pages, which do not belong in the search index; this is another reason it is kept separate from Googlebot.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
author: Google Merchant Center Help
label: docs
text: Google's Merchant Center help says the StoreBot crawler goes through product detail, cart and checkout pages, can fill in checkout forms, and records price, shipping, availability, coupons and payment methods to verify the data merchants share in Merchant Center.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
author: Google
label: docs
text: Google's crawler list says robots.txt rules addressed to the Storebot-Google user agent affect all surfaces of Google Shopping, such as the Shopping tab in Google Search.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Treat Storebot-Google separately from Googlebot in robots.txt and bot protection: a shop that blocks it on product, cart or checkout paths can undermine Shopping price and availability checks, even when Googlebot is allowed.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Product Q&A can be marked up in schema.org by linking Question items, each with an acceptedAnswer of type Answer, to the product through the subjectOf property, because the product is the subject of the Q&A.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Google now emphasises two existing Merchant Center attributes for AI, product highlights (a short bulleted list) and product detail (detailed specifications), and updated its Help Center guidance to say they help AI systems.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
author: Google Merchant Center Help
label: docs
text: Merchant Center's product_highlight attribute takes 2 to 100 highlights of up to 150 characters each that describe only the product itself, without promotional text, keywords or search terms.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Instead of adding feed attributes for individual specifications such as connectivity, memory, camera settings or box contents, Google asks merchants to send them as key-value pairs in product detail, because merchants know best what matters.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
author: Google Merchant Center Help
label: docs
text: Merchant Center's product_detail attribute takes up to 100 specifications, each a section name, attribute name and attribute value, and Google's help says clean key-value specifications improve product details on Google Shopping and AI-driven surfaces.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Google works to make sure that what merchants can express in its shopping feeds can also be expressed in schema.org, adding vocabulary where schema.org lacks it, for example for product details.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Google named the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), next to the Merchant Center feed, as an industry standard whose capabilities it also wants schema.org to cover.

sources.title: New tech and tools for retailers to succeed in an agentic shopping era

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
author: Google blog (11 January 2026)
label: docs
text: Google launched the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) on 11 January 2026 as an open standard for agentic commerce across discovery, buying and post-purchase support, co-developed with retailers and platforms and compatible with A2A, AP2 and MCP.

sources.title: New tech and tools for retailers to succeed in an agentic shopping era

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: A recent schema.org release added two properties, specification and valueGroup, so that the Merchant Center product detail attribute can be expressed in schema.org, with product specs nested under specification.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Schema.org's release notes show version 30.1 (16 September 2026) added specification, isOftenBoughtWith and consumerNotice for Product, valueGroup for PropertyValue and itemPopularity for Offer as vocabulary for retail feed data; Google's Search Central docs did not yet document these properties on 3 October 2026.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Rich, lightly structured information is critical to AI systems: product data with many levels of nesting is not needed, but some structure is very important.
quote: rich, lightly structured information is critical to AI systems.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Basic, well-specified product attributes such as price, brand and availability remain as important as ever for Google Shopping.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Rich, less structured product data that is not prescribed by Google, schema.org or any feed or data model is increasingly important, because the merchant or brand knows best what to provide.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: The bar for product data quality is higher than ever because agents and users need correct information: with wrong data an agent might buy the wrong product for a user.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Web markup is an efficient and unambiguous way for sites to share product data with Google, Google Shopping said, repeating the Day 2 structured data talk.

sources.title: Introduction to structured data markup in Google Search

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Google Shopping named the downside of adding Q&As and documentation to product markup: the page's markup becomes somewhat bigger.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Google Shopping pointed to a Google holiday shopping blog post with early results from real merchants using the conversational attributes, and to the Merchant Center Help Center and schema.org for the attributes and properties.

sources.title: Boost your holiday sales with these agentic commerce updates

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
author: Google blog (16 September 2026)
label: docs
text: Google's 16 September 2026 holiday shopping post says that in testing with lululemon, conversational attributes submitted by the brand were used 50% of the time in relevant product recommendations in AI Mode.

sources.title: Boost your holiday sales with these agentic commerce updates

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
speaker: Alex Jansen
label: stage
text: Google Shopping described product data for AI as early days in a fast-moving area, with many more changes to come.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Shop developers should first keep core feed and markup values (price, availability, brand, GTIN) accurate, then add Q&As, product highlights, specs as key-value product details and related products in the Merchant Center feed, and mirror them in schema.org Product markup only as Google documents support for it.

session: Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Content teams can feed the new Q&A attribute from real customer questions (support tickets, reviews, sales chats), answered factually per product; this is the detailed, merchant-owned data Google said AI shopping answers need.

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: stage
text: Google's Search Console talk at the Deep Dive covered five Search Console launches of the past year: query groups, AI-powered configuration of the Performance report, generative AI control and reporting, platform properties for social accounts, and multimodal search reporting.

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: stage
text: Search Console's query groups put together queries that express a very similar user intent but are written differently, for example with more or fewer words or with spelling errors, so site owners can see the intent behind their traffic instead of every query string.

sources.title: Introducing Query groups in Search Console Insights

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: slide
text: To show how diverse queries for one intent are, Google's Search Console talk showed a slide titled 'How to spell Britney Spears?' with a long list of spelling variants, citing archive.google/jobs/britney.html.
quote: How to spell Britney Spears?

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: stage
text: Google's Search Console talk said Google's logs show hundreds of different ways in which people write the query for Britney Spears.

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: The Google archive page cited on the Britney Spears slide lists 593 spellings (the correct one plus 592 misspellings), each typed by at least two different users within a three-month period and corrected by Google's spelling system; it is an old jobs page (footer 2011), so the figures are historical.

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: stage
text: Google said query groups are not built by matching query text alone: deciding which queries belong in which group goes beyond simple text filtering.

sources.title: Introducing Query groups in Search Console Insights

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: stage
text: Google named granularity as a design challenge of query groups: putting many queries into one large group versus splitting them into smaller, more specific groups.

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: stage
text: Query groups can change when the meaning of a query changes over time: a 2023 search for 'Gemini' may have meant the astrological sign, but after Google launched Gemini it means something else, so Search Console may now group it differently.

sources.title: Introducing Query groups in Search Console Insights

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: stage
text: Google acknowledged that query grouping is not perfect: some queries are not understood, and some are not grouped in a logical way.

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: stage
text: Query groups appear in the Search Console Insights report as a table of the top groups, showing the total clicks of all the queries inside each group, with an option to view a larger table.

sources.title: Introducing Query groups in Search Console Insights

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: stage
text: Each query group in Search Console is titled with the most prominent query in the group.

sources.title: Introducing Query groups in Search Console Insights

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: stage
text: Drilling into a query group opens the Search Console Performance report with a regex filter that contains all the queries of the group, so each individual query can be analysed.

sources.title: Introducing Query groups in Search Console Insights
Performance report (Search results): Advanced filtering and comparison

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: stage
text: Google's Search Console team said query groups have been found very useful and that people are using them.

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: stage
text: Google's Search Console team asks for feedback on every new feature, through the thumbs up and thumbs down buttons or any other feedback feature in Search Console, and said it takes that feedback very seriously.

sources.title: Introducing Query groups in Search Console Insights

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: The speaker placed the query groups launch, hedging, in December, but Google's announcement is dated 27 October 2025 with a gradual rollout over the following weeks, so many sites may first have seen the card around December 2025.

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: For content planning, read query groups (and their trending up and trending down views) as intent themes: write for the intent the group stands for, not for each spelling or phrasing variant in it.

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: stage
text: Users often told Google that the Search Console Performance report is complex to configure, because it can be filtered and customised in many ways, such as by query, page, country and search type.

sources.title: Streamline your Search Console analysis with the new AI-powered configuration

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: stage
text: Search Console's AI-powered configuration is a chat box in which users describe the analysis they want in natural language, and the request is transformed into the Performance report's configuration.

sources.title: Streamline your Search Console analysis with the new AI-powered configuration
Performance report (Search results): Advanced filtering and comparison

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: stage
text: Google said requests to Search Console's AI-powered configuration can be written in any language, not only English.

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: stage
text: Search Console's AI-powered configuration lists the changes it will make to the Performance report and applies them only after the user approves.

sources.title: Performance report (Search results): Advanced filtering and comparison

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: stage

sources.title: Performance report (Search results): Advanced filtering and comparison

sources.title: Streamline your Search Console analysis with the new AI-powered configuration

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It

label: stage

sources.title: Performance report (Search results): Advanced filtering and comparison

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
author: Ibrahim Anjro

text: Review the filters and regexes that Search Console's AI-powered configuration proposes before trusting the numbers: Google's launch post calls the feature experimental, warns that AI can misinterpret requests, and limits it to the Search results Performance report (not Discover or News) and to configuration, not sorting or exporting.

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: stage
text: Search Console has a tool with which every property owner can tell Google whether the site's content may be used in AI search results, because Google wants content owners to control their content.

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
speaker: Ariel Kroszynski
label: stage

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It

sources.title: Introducing Search Generative AI performance reports in Search Console

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It

author: Search Central blog (27 October 2025)

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
author: Google Search Console Help
label: docs

sources.title: About platform properties in Search Console

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
author: Google Search Console Help

text: Google's help page says platform properties show only how content performs on Google Search, Discover and Google News, not how often it is seen on the social or video platform itself.

sources.title: About platform properties in Search Console

session: Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It
author: Google Search Central
label: docs
text: Google's social and video performance guide says that if you already claimed your Search profile, all of its verified accounts are added automatically as platform properties in Search Console.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users

label: stage
text: In a community lightning talk, agency founder Nik Vujic presented how his agency feeds Search Console and GA4 data to an LLM agent to support decisions for its clients.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: stage
text: Nik Vujic called Google Search Console his favourite SEO tool, used alongside GA4, and said third-party SEO tools give only estimates, although they have some use cases.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: stage
text: Nik Vujic said it is super important to export all of a site's Search Console data, and his agency's workflow starts from Search Console's export to BigQuery.

sources.title: About bulk data export of Search Console data to BigQuery

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: slide
text: A community slide (Workflow 1) said the first step is to apply the filters you need, even natively in Search Console, for example branded versus non-branded queries, with clicks and impressions.

sources.title: Introducing the branded queries filter in Search Console
sources.publisher: Search Central blog (20 November 2025, updated 11 March 2026)

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
author: Search Central blog (20 November 2025, updated 11 March 2026)
label: docs
text: Google's launch post for Search Console's branded queries filter (20 November 2025) says the branded versus non-branded split is made by an internal AI-assisted system, not by a regular expression, and that some queries may occasionally be misidentified.

sources.title: Introducing the branded queries filter in Search Console
sources.publisher: Search Central blog (20 November 2025, updated 11 March 2026)

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: slide

quote: The UI export is limited to 1,000 rows.

sources.title: A deep dive into Search Console performance data filtering and limits

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: slide
text: A community slide said the Search Console bulk data export to BigQuery gives the most complete query dataset available, with anonymized queries excluded.
quote: The bulk export to BigQuery gives the most complete query dataset available - anonymized queries excluded.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: In the bulk export, 'anonymized queries excluded' means the query text, not the traffic: Google's table reference and query guidelines show those rows kept with an empty query field, often as the single most common 'query'. Tell an LLM to skip empty queries when ranking top queries, but keep them in totals.

sources.title: About bulk data export of Search Console data to BigQuery

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: slide
text: The community workflow's third step feeds the exported Search Console dataset into the agency's LLM agent, which queries the dataset and returns the evidence rather than a sample.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: slide
text: Nik Vujic's slide said no agent is needed to start: pull the Search Console data, import it into any LLM and query it in conversation; his agency built its agent to have everything in one place.
quote: No agent needed to start: pull the data and import it into the LLM of your choice, and talk with it.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: stage

sources.title: A deep dive into Search Console performance data filtering and limits

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users

sources.title: A deep dive into Search Console performance data filtering and limits

sources.title: A deep dive into Search Console performance data filtering and limits

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: stage
text: Nik Vujic said his agency uses the Search Console data fed to an LLM in five use cases, the first being cross-comparing and following up different articles.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: stage
text: Nik Vujic said that after a page is published, the queries it appears for are the first thing to show up in Search Console, while clicks and impressions come much later.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: A query reaches Search Console's Performance report only through an impression, so queries cannot come before impressions; what rises first after a publish or refresh is the number of queries with a few impressions each, before total impressions and clicks grow noticeably.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: stage
text: To report content refreshes on large sites, Nik Vujic's agency compares date ranges and has an LLM give the exact number of queries the content improved on, then reports that number to the client.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: stage
text: Nik Vujic said Google loves fresh, quality content, as a reason for large sites to refresh their content.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Google's ranking systems guide describes 'query deserves freshness' systems that show fresher content where it would be expected, which is narrower than a general preference for fresh content; refresh pages whose queries expect current information, and judge other refreshes by quality.

sources.title: A guide to Google Search ranking systems

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: stage
text: Nik Vujic said analysing Search Console query data with an LLM also helped his agency spot developer mistakes, such as unwanted pages that got indexed, which can also be found in Search Console itself.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: stage
text: Nik Vujic said some keyword cannibalization is fine because it is logical, but for bad cannibalization his agency groups all of an article's Search Console queries and then decides whether to redirect the pages or rewrite and split the content.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: stage
text: Nik Vujic advised starting every SEO experiment with a hypothesis, for example a bulk change to one page element across a group of pages, and using an LLM to report the group's Search Console data, for example click-through rate, for the test.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: stage
text: Nik Vujic called the GA4 API combined with Looker Studio the only LLM traffic tracker that actually works.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: stage
text: Nik Vujic said GA4 setups that separate out traffic from LLMs do not capture visits from AI Overviews and AI Mode.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: stage
text: Nik Vujic said Google Tag Manager events can be used to follow real traffic arriving from different LLMs.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: stage
text: Nik Vujic's agency puts Search Console data, LLM referral traffic from GA4 and the data from Search Console's generative AI report into one LLM prompt to compare a client's performance in classic search and in AI features.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: stage
text: Nik Vujic said he hopes Search Console's generative AI report will get query data.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
speaker: Nik Vujic
label: stage
text: Nik Vujic said his agency uses the combined data to test whether good SEO is good GEO, and that the answer is 'it depends': for one client it found pages that performed better in generative AI features and LLMs than in standard search.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Pages that do better in AI answers than in classic results do not refute Google's line that optimising for people is optimising for generative AI Search, since the comparison mixed Google's AI features with third-party LLMs; measure each surface separately, per page, before deciding what to change.

sources.title: Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
author: Google Search Central

text: Google's AI features guide says traffic from sites appearing in AI features such as AI Overviews and AI Mode is included in the overall search traffic in Search Console and reported in the Performance report within the Web search type.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
author: Search Central blog (20 November 2025, updated 11 March 2026)
label: docs
text: Search Console's branded queries filter works only for top-level properties, not URL-path or subdomain properties, and only for sites with enough queries and impressions; Google made it available to all eligible sites on 11 March 2026.

sources.title: Introducing the branded queries filter in Search Console
sources.publisher: Search Central blog (20 November 2025, updated 11 March 2026)

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Because Google says anonymized queries are left out whenever a filter is applied, branded plus non-branded exports should not be expected to add up to the unfiltered chart totals; tell an LLM that sums filtered exports that the gap is expected, not missing data.

sources.title: A deep dive into Search Console performance data filtering and limits

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users
author: Ibrahim Anjro
label: analysis
text: Before feeding a branded versus non-branded split to an LLM, spot-check a sample of queries in each group, since Google's AI-assisted classification can misidentify queries; on URL-path or subdomain properties, where the filter is unavailable, a regex query filter is the fallback.

sources.title: Introducing the branded queries filter in Search Console
sources.publisher: Search Central blog (20 November 2025, updated 11 March 2026)

text: Looker Studio lifts Search Console's 1,000-row interface limit but keeps the connector's cap of 50,000 rows per day per site per search type; only the bulk export to BigQuery is free of the daily row limit, so large sites that need every non-anonymized query should use it.

text: The click decline described on stage is what many individual sites report, while Google's published position (August 2025) is that total organic clicks are relatively stable but shifting between sites, with fewer clicks for quick-answer questions; neither side gave figures, so measure the trend per site and per query type rather than assuming a market-wide fall.

sources.title: AI in Search is driving more queries and higher quality clicks

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users

label: stage
text: In data a community speaker tracks for particular brands, local search terms have started to lose clicks too as AI features appear on more results pages.

session: Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users

speaker: unknown
